source_refs.note: Book p. 72: 3.1.1 Rule-1 (constant), Rule-2 (sum and difference), Rule-3 (power rule), the General Power Rule, Rule-4 (f'/f) and Rule-5 (linear substitution).

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein humne andaza laga kar antiderivatives nikaale the: 'kis function ka derivative \(3x^{2}\) hai?' Lekin har baar andaza lagana na aasan hai na mehfooz. Is liye aaj hum integration ke paanch buniyadi rules aur ek General Power Rule seekhenge. Achhi khabar yeh hai ke yeh sab rules aap pehle se jaante hain, bas ulte roop mein: har rule differentiation ke kisi rule ko ulta parhne se bana hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Har rule ko yaad karne ka sab se pakka tareeqa: right-hand side ko differentiate kar ke dekhiye, integrand wapas aa jayega. Yani rule ke saath us ki 'tasdeeq' bhi yaad kijiye. Is tarah agar exam hall mein koi rule bhool bhi jaye to aap use khud dobara bana sakte hain.
Pehla rule sab se seedha hai, aur yeh constant (yani woh number jo badalta nahin) ke baare mein hai. Kitab mein yeh is tarah likha hai:
Rule-1: \(\int k\,f(x)\,dx = k\int f(x)\,dx\) (Integration of function with constant (k)).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun: differentiation mein \(\frac{d}{dx}\big(k\,F(x)\big) = k\,F'(x)\) hota hai, yani constant bahar khara rehta hai. Is liye integration mein bhi constant bahar nikal aata hai.
Kab: jab integrand ke aage koi number (ya constant letter jaise \(a\), \(k\)) zarb ho.
Hamari misaal: \(\int 5x^{2}\,dx = 5\int x^{2}\,dx = 5 \cdot \frac{x^{3}}{3} + c = \frac{5}{3}x^{3} + c\). Yahan 5 ko bahar rakh kar sirf \(x^{2}\) ka integral liya.
Dhyan dein: sirf constant bahar nikalta hai. \(\int x \cdot x\,dx\) ko \(x\int x\,dx\) likhna ghalat hai, kyun ke \(x\) constant nahin, badalta rehta hai. Jaise dukaan par har cheez par 10 rupay tax ho to tax ko bahar le ja sakte hain, magar jo cheez har item ke saath badalti ho use bahar nahin le ja sakte.
Doosra rule batata hai ke jab integrand mein kai terms jama ya tafreeq (minus) ho rahe hon to kya karna hai. Is rule ki wajah se lamba integrand chhote chhote aasan tukron mein toot jata hai:
Rule-2: \(\int [f(x) \pm g(x)]\,dx = \int f(x)\,dx \pm \int g(x)\,dx\) (Sum and Difference Rule).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun: sum ka derivative, derivatives ka sum hota hai. Is liye sum ka integral bhi term by term (har term alag alag) liya ja sakta hai.
Kab: jab integrand kai terms ka ho jo \(+\) ya \(-\) se jure hon. Har term ka alag integral lein aur aakhir mein sirf ek \(+\,c\) likhein, kyun ke sab terms ke constants mil kar ek hi constant ban jate hain.
Hamari misaal: \(\int (6x^{2} - \cos x)\,dx = 2x^{3} - \sin x + c\). Pehle term se \(2x^{3}\), doosre se \(-\sin x\).
Dhyan dein: product (zarb) ke liye aisa koi rule nahin. \(\int x \cdot x\,dx = \frac{x^{3}}{3} + c\) hai, magar \(\int x\,dx \cdot \int x\,dx\) se \(\frac{x^{4}}{4}\) aayega, jo ghalat hai. Product ho to pehle multiply kar ke terms bana lein (ya aage aane wale tareeqe istemal karein).
Ab sab se zyada istemal hone wala rule aata hai, power rule. Is unit ke taqreeban har sawal mein yeh kahin na kahin lagega, is liye ise khoob pakka kar lijiye:
Rule-3: \(\int x^{n}\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + c\), where \(n \ne -1\) (The Power Rule).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun: jawab ko differentiate kar ke dekhiye:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\right) = \dfrac{(n+1)x^{n}}{n+1}\]
\[= x^{n}\]
Lafzon mein: power mein 1 jama karo, phir nayi power se divide karo. Yeh derivative wale rule 'power se zarb do, phir power mein se 1 kam karo' ka bilkul ulta hai. Ulta kaam ulti tarteeb mein hota hai, jaise joote pehle utaarte hain phir jurabein.
\(n \ne -1\) kyun? Kyun ke \(n = -1\) par nayi power 0 ban jati hai aur 0 se divide karna mumkin nahin. Yeh khaas case \(\int \frac{1}{x}\,dx = \ln|x| + c\) hai, jo 3.1.2 ki table mein aata hai.
Yeh rule har real \(n \ne -1\) ke liye chalta hai: negative aur fraction wali powers ke liye bhi. Bas pehle roots aur reciprocals ko power ki shakal mein likh lein, jaise \(\sqrt{x} = x^{1/2}\) aur \(\frac{1}{x^{3}} = x^{-3}\).
Hamari misaalein: \(\int x^{4}\,dx = \frac{x^{5}}{5} + c\); \(\int x^{-3}\,dx = \frac{x^{-2}}{-2} + c = -\frac{1}{2x^{2}} + c\); \(\int \sqrt{x}\,dx = \int x^{1/2}\,dx = \frac{x^{3/2}}{3/2} + c = \frac{2}{3}x^{3/2} + c\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{x^{3/2}}{3/2}\) ko \(\frac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\) likhna, yani fraction se divide karna us ke ulte se zarb dena hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Sawal: \(\int 1\,dx\) power rule se kya banta hai?
Jawab: \(1 = x^{0}\), to \(n = 0\): \(\int x^{0}\,dx = \frac{x^{1}}{1} + c = x + c\). Yahi 3.1.2 ki table ki doosri row hai.
Power rule mein sirf akela \(x\) power par tha. Lekin agar poora bracket power par ho to? Is ke liye kitab General Power Rule deti hai:
The General Power Rule: \(\int [f(x)]^{n} f'(x)\,dx = \frac{[f(x)]^{n+1}}{n+1} + c\), where \(n \ne -1\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun: chain rule se,
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{[f(x)]^{n+1}}{n+1}\right) = [f(x)]^{n} f'(x)\]
Yahan bracket ki power neeche aati hai aur bracket ke andar wale ka derivative \(f'(x)\) saath zarb ho jata hai.
Kab: jab aap ko ek bracket kisi power par nazar aaye, aur saath us bracket ke andar wale hisse ka derivative zarb ho. Tab poore bracket ko ek 'bara \(x\)' samajh kar power rule laga dein.
Hamari misaalein: \(\int (x^{2} + 1)^{3}\,2x\,dx = \frac{(x^{2} + 1)^{4}}{4} + c\), kyun ke \(2x\), \(x^{2} + 1\) ka derivative hai. Isi tarah \(\int (x^{3} + 5)^{2}\,3x^{2}\,dx = \frac{(x^{3} + 5)^{3}}{3} + c\).
Dhyan dein: agar bracket ka derivative maujood na ho to yeh rule nahin lagta. \(\int (x^{2} + 1)^{3}\,dx\) ka jawab \(\frac{(x^{2} + 1)^{4}}{4} + c\) nahin; is ko pehle khol (expand) kar term by term integrate karein.
Ab woh case jo power rule nahin sambhal sakta tha, yani jab power \(-1\) ho. Is ke liye logarithm wala rule hai:
Rule-4: \(\int \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx = \ln|f(x)| + c\)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun: chain rule se \(\frac{d}{dx}\ln|f(x)| = \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\).
Kab: jab integrand ek fraction ho aur us ka numerator (upar wala hissa) denominator (neeche wale hisse) ka derivative ho. Yeh General Power Rule ka \(n = -1\) wala case hai, jo power rule se nahin ho sakta tha.
Pehchaan ka tareeqa: neeche wale ko differentiate kijiye; agar upar wala mil jaye to jawab '\(\ln|\)neeche wala\(|\) \(+\,c\)' hai.
Hamari misaal: \(\int \frac{2x}{x^{2} + 5}\,dx = \ln|x^{2} + 5| + c = \ln(x^{2} + 5) + c\), kyun ke \(x^{2} + 5\) hamesha positive hai.
Agar numerator derivative ka sirf koi hissa ho (constant ka farq) to Rule-1 se constant theek kar lein: \(\int \frac{x}{x^{2} + 5}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{x^{2} + 5}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\ln(x^{2} + 5) + c\). Yahan humne andar 2 se zarb kiya aur bahar \(\frac{1}{2}\) se, to value wahi rahi.
Absolute value kyun? Kyun ke \(\ln\) sirf positive numbers ka hota hai, jab ke \(f(x)\) negative bhi ho sakta hai.
Aakhri rule tab kaam aata hai jab \(x\) ki jagah \(3x + 2\) ya \(2x - 1\) jaisi seedhi (linear) expression baithi ho:

Rule-5: If \(f'\) is the derivative of \(f\), and \(\int f'(x)\,dx = f(x) + c\), then for any constants \(a \ne 0\) and \(b\), \(\int f'(ax+b)\,dx = \frac{f(ax+b)}{a} + c\). (Linear Substitution Rule).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun: chain rule se \(\frac{d}{dx}f(ax+b) = a\,f'(ax+b)\). Differentiate karne se ek extra \(a\) bahar aa jata hai; is liye integration mein us \(a\) se divide karna parta hai, taa ke wapas differentiate karein to \(a\) cancel ho jaye.
Kab: jab koi aisa function ho jis ka integral aap jaante hain, magar \(x\) ki jagah ek linear expression \(ax + b\) baitha ho.
Hamari misaalein: \(\int \cos(3x + 2)\,dx = \frac{\sin(3x + 2)}{3} + c\); \(\int (2x + 1)^{5}\,dx = \frac{(2x + 1)^{6}}{6 \cdot 2} + c = \frac{(2x + 1)^{6}}{12} + c\); \(\int e^{4x - 1}\,dx = \frac{e^{4x - 1}}{4} + c\).
Dhyan dein: yeh sirf linear andar wale (\(ax + b\)) ke liye hai. \(\int \cos(x^{2})\,dx\) mein \(x^{2}\) ke derivative se divide kar dena ghalat hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Sawal: \(\int \sin(5x)\,dx\) kya hoga?
Jawab: \(\int \sin x\,dx = -\cos x + c\), aur andar \(5x\) hai (\(a = 5\)), to \(\int \sin 5x\,dx = -\frac{\cos 5x}{5} + c\). Tasdeeq: \(\frac{d}{dx}\left(-\frac{\cos 5x}{5}\right) = \frac{5\sin 5x}{5} = \sin 5x\).
Ab sab rules ko ek jagah dekh lete hain, taa ke sawal dekh kar foran pehchaan sakein ke kaunsa rule lagana hai:

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Rule-1: constant integral se bahar aata hai. Rule-2: term by term integrate karo.
2. Rule-3 (power rule): \(\int x^{n}\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + c\), \(n \ne -1\); power mein 1 jama karo, nayi power se divide karo.
3. General Power Rule: bracket ki power zarb bracket ka derivative.
4. Rule-4: numerator = denominator ka derivative ho to jawab \(\ln|\text{denominator}| + c\).
5. Rule-5: andar \(ax + b\) ho to aam tarah integrate karo aur \(a\) se divide karo.
6. Har jawab ko differentiate kar ke check karo.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Product ko tor dena: \(\int f(x)g(x)\,dx \ne \int f(x)\,dx \cdot \int g(x)\,dx\).
2. \(n = -1\) par power rule lagana: \(\int x^{-1}\,dx = \ln|x| + c\) hai, \(\frac{x^{0}}{0}\) kabhi nahin.
3. Rule-5 mein \(a\) se divide karna bhool jana: \(\int (2x+1)^{5}\,dx \ne \frac{(2x+1)^{6}}{6} + c\); sahi \(\frac{(2x+1)^{6}}{12} + c\).
4. Rule-4 tab lagana jab upar wala neeche wale ka derivative na ho: \(\int \frac{1}{x^{2} + 1}\,dx \ne \ln(x^{2} + 1) + c\) (yeh \(\tan^{-1}x + c\) hai, 3.1.2 dekhiye).
5. \(f'(x)\) maujood na ho phir bhi General Power Rule lagana: \(\int (x^{2} + 1)^{3}\,dx \ne \frac{(x^{2} + 1)^{4}}{4} + c\).
